steps.title: Personal fouls
steps.body: Illegal contact, like ==pushing, holding or hitting a shooter's arm==, is a personal foul. Fouls decide close games because they give away ==free points==.

steps.title: Shooting fouls
steps.body: Fouled while shooting and you miss? You get ==free throws==: ==3 if you were shooting a three==, 2 for anything else.

steps.title: And one
steps.body: Make the shot while getting fouled and ==the basket still counts==. You also get ==1 free throw==. Fans and announcers call it an and-one.

steps.title: Block or charge
steps.body: A driver runs into a defender. If the defender was ==set before the contact==, it's a charge on the offense. If the defender was still sliding in, it's a ==blocking foul==.
steps.note: One of the hardest calls in sports. Replays rarely settle it.

steps.title: The bonus
steps.body: Once a team commits ==5 fouls in a quarter==, every foul after that sends the other team to the line. That's called being ==in the bonus==.

steps.title: Fouling out
steps.body: A pro player who commits ==6 personal fouls== has to sit for the rest of the game. In college it's 5. Stars in foul trouble often ==sit early to stay safe==.

steps.prompt: The defender got there first. What's the call?
steps.explain: The defender was set in the driver's path before the contact, so the driver is called for a charge. Any basket wouldn't count.

steps.prompt: A player is fouled shooting a three and misses. How many free throws?
steps.explain: Free throws match the shot: fouled on a three-point attempt means 3 free throws.
